title: Best Midea Dehumidifier (2026): Cube, 35-Pint & Pump Models
h1: The Best Midea Dehumidifiers: Every Cube Model Ranked
dek: One clever design in three sizes, plus an upright 50-pint with a pump. The trick is picking the model that matches your room, not the biggest box on the shelf.
description: The best Midea dehumidifier for your space: the Cube 20, 35 and 50-pint models and Midea's 50-pint pump unit ranked, plus filter, manual and error-code help.
intro: Shopping for the best Midea dehumidifier? Start with the **Cube**, the design that changed what a portable dehumidifier looks like. Instead of a small pull-out bucket tucked into a tall cabinet, the whole lower half of the machine is the water reservoir. The top section sits nested inside it for shipping and storage, then lifts and twists up to expose a tank big enough that you can go days, not hours, between emptying.

The lineup is refreshingly simple: a 20-pint, a 35-pint and a 50-pint Cube, plus a conventional upright 50-pint model with a built-in pump for basements that sit below the nearest drain. The Cubes share the same app, the same set-a-number humidistat and ENERGY STAR certification, and the pump model is ENERGY STAR certified with app control too, so choosing one comes down to two questions — how much space are you drying, and where does the water need to go?
We compared every current Cube using ENERGY STAR's certified-product data, Midea's coverage ratings and manuals, and patterns in owner reviews. Here's how they rank, and which one fits your room.
topPicksLead: For most homes, the **Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT)** is the one to buy: it covers a whole basement or main floor and costs only a little more than the 35-pint model.

products.whyWeLoveIt: The Cube 50 removes the biggest daily annoyance of owning a dehumidifier: the bucket. Its reservoir base stores several ordinary buckets' worth of water, so a damp basement doesn't mean a twice-a-day trip downstairs. And because the price gap to the 35-pint model is small, it's the smart default when you're not sure how much capacity you need.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR lists it at 49.67 pints a day under the current DOE test, an integrated energy factor of 2.01 liters per kWh and 515 kWh a year. That efficiency sits right at the certification line for 50-pint units, in line with rivals rather than ahead of them. Owners consistently describe fast pull-down in musty basements and praise the app for checking humidity without going downstairs. Prefer to skip the tank entirely? Run the included hose to a floor drain.
products.notes: If the unit will sit below your nearest drain, as in most basements, skip to the pump model below.

This Midea's built-in pump lifts water up to a utility sink or out a basement window, turning it into a machine you can genuinely leave alone for the season.
products.performance: Midea rates it at 50 pints a day with ENERGY STAR certification and coverage up to 4,500 square feet, matching the Cube 50 on paper. The difference is the body and the water handling: it's a traditional upright cabinet rather than a Cube, and it pumps water away instead of storing it in a big reservoir base. For any space you don't walk through daily, that convenience is worth it. Compare it with other self-draining machines in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.
products.notes: Check the pump hose for kinks after setup; a pinched line is the most common reason pump units stop and flash an error.

Because the two are often priced close together, sizing up is usually the better bet if your space is borderline — a slightly larger unit cycles less and holds its setpoint more easily. It's also a strong pick for a [finished basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-finished-basement/) with carpet and furniture.

It also anchors our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) picks.

sections.heading: How we pick the best Midea dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't run a test lab. Instead, we start with the numbers that are comparable across every brand: capacity and integrated energy factor under the 2019 DOE test procedure, as published in ENERGY STAR's certified-product dataset. We then check Midea's own coverage claims and manuals for drainage options, humidistat range and warranty terms, and scan the CPSC database for recalls.

Finally, we read owner reviews in bulk, looking for repeated patterns rather than one-off complaints: reservoirs that leak at the seam, sensors that read well off a standalone hygrometer, pumps that fail early. Because the Cube line shares one design, the ranking is less about which model is "better" and more about which size and drainage setup fits which space. Weighing Midea against its closest rival? See our [Midea vs. Frigidaire](/compare/midea-vs-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) comparison.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Midea dehumidifier

items.label: Coverage, not the pint label
items.text: DOE ratings changed in 2019 and now run lower than old labels. Use Midea's square-footage rating and our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) to match the Cube to your space.

items.label: A pump only if you need one
items.text: If there's a floor drain below the unit, the standard Cube and its gravity hose are fine. If the water has to go up — to a sink or out a window — buy the pump model.

items.label: Reservoir or hose, pick one
items.text: The big base is perfect for a room you pass every day. For a space you rarely visit, connect the hose and treat the reservoir as a backup.

items.label: App control where it counts
items.text: Wi-Fi matters most for basements and crawl-space-adjacent rooms. Being alerted to a full tank or a humidity spike saves a lot of stairs.

items.label: Warranty awareness
items.text: Midea covers the Cube for one year. Buy from a retailer with a generous return window, and register the unit so you're covered if an early fault appears.

sections.heading: Older Midea models: the MAD50PS1WS and the 22-pint

blocks.text: Midea sold conventional box-style dehumidifiers long before the Cube, and two of them still turn up constantly in searches and on store shelves.

The **MAD50PS1WS** is an older version of Midea's traditional upright 50-pint unit with a built-in pump — the same format as the current pump model we pick above, lifting water to a sink or out a window from an ordinary cabinet rather than a Cube's reservoir base. If you find one at a good price it's still a capable basement machine; just confirm the listing's capacity rating is under the current DOE test, and check that it's new stock with a full warranty rather than an open-box return.

The **MAD22C1AWS** is Midea's compact ENERGY STAR box for a bedroom, office or laundry room. It's a sensible alternative to the Cube 20 if you'd rather have a conventional shape, and the related *smart* 22-pint versions add Wi-Fi app control. Both sizes suit a single room, not a whole basement.

sections.heading: Midea dehumidifier manual, filter and repair help

blocks.text: Most Midea service calls come down to a handful of simple fixes. Your user manual — downloadable from Midea's support site by model number — is the final word, but here's what owners run into most.

blocks.text: For anything beyond these, such as a compressor that won't start or a refrigerant smell, stop using the unit and contact Midea support while it's under warranty. Routine care, from filter washing to coil cleaning, is covered in our [dehumidifier maintenance](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) guide.

The **Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT)** is the best Midea dehumidifier for most homes: full basement-grade capacity, a reservoir that cuts down on emptying, and app control, for only slightly more than the 35-pint. Choose the **Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump** if the unit sits below your drain, the **Cube 35** for a mid-size space, and the **Cube 20** for a single bedroom or office. Just keep the one-year warranty in mind and buy where returns are easy. For the wider field, start with our [best dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier/) roundup.

faqs.q: What is the best Midea dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For most homes, the Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT). ENERGY STAR rates it at 49.67 DOE pints a day and Midea says it covers up to about 4,500 sq ft. Choose Midea's upright 50-pint with pump if the unit sits below the nearest drain, or the Cube 20 for a single bedroom.

faqs.q: What's the difference between the Cube 50 and Midea's 50-pint with pump?
faqs.a: Mostly the water handling and the body. Both are rated at 50 pints a day, ENERGY STAR certified and rated for up to 4,500 sq ft. The Cube 50 stores water in its large reservoir base or drains downhill through a gravity hose; the pump model is a conventional upright unit that can push water up to a sink or out a basement window, so it can run unattended where there's no low drain.

faqs.q: How many square feet does a Midea 35-pint dehumidifier cover?
faqs.a: Midea rates the Cube 35 for up to about 3,000 sq ft. For comparison, the Cube 20 covers about 1,500 sq ft and the Cube 50 up to 4,500 sq ft. Real-world coverage depends on how damp the space is, so size up for a wet basement.

faqs.q: Are Midea Cube dehumidifier reviews good?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. Owner reviews of the Cube consistently praise the big reservoir and app control. The most common complaints are the one-year warranty and occasional Wi-Fi setup hiccups, so buy from a retailer with an easy return policy.

faqs.q: What does P2 mean on a Midea dehumidifier?
faqs.a: On Midea units, P2 almost always means the bucket is full or isn't seated properly. Empty it, push it firmly back into place, and the code should clear. If it persists with an empty tank, check your manual and contact Midea support.

faqs.q: Why is the filter light blinking on my Midea dehumidifier?
faqs.a: It's a cleaning reminder that comes on after a set number of running hours. Slide out the filter, rinse it in warm water, let it dry completely, reinstall it and press the filter button to reset the light.

faqs.q: Has there been a Midea dehumidifier recall?
faqs.a: The best-known dehumidifier recalls of the past decade involved units from other manufacturers, such as Gree and New Widetech. To check any Midea model, search its exact model number on CPSC.gov and on Midea's support site before buying used or older stock.
